practiceNotes: This is a curriculum proposal for human review. Flashcards support retrieval and discrimination; proofs, programming, experiments, and research judgment require the extended practice specified.

Chemical, biological, and physical experiments require supervision, local risk assessment, facility procedures, and approved waste handling; none of these external conditions is represented as satisfied.

Radioactive sources, regulated biological materials, lasers, cryogens, and high-power equipment require facility-specific training and authorization. Supplied datasets and simulations offer alternatives.
Human-participant, animal, field-collection, and sensitive genomic work may require ethics approval, consent, permits, privacy safeguards, and data-use agreements.
Security exercises must use owned or explicitly authorized systems. Educational cryptographic implementations are not deployment recommendations.
Embedded and robotics practice should begin in simulation or supervised low-energy hardware. Educational success does not establish safety certification.
Drug-discovery, physiology, and epidemiology exercises do not authorize prescribing, clinical treatment, or operational public-health decisions.
Computational projects require suitable software and computing access; platform-specific installation and facility procedures should be selected during implementation.
